clue.text: Cancel escape into outer part

indicators.note: into says the escape piece goes inside the outer part

parts.note: the rind is the outer part of fruit or cheese
ESC is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a breakout through the perimeter of a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or order is to revoke it, a synonym.

clue.text: Genuine about short urban performance

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for genuine surrounds the other piece

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: short says the word drops its last letter

parts.note: city means urban, as in city life

explanation.surface: A real recital about a brief trip to town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts CITY to CIT, which 'about' puts inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: Allowance cut -it can only just support one

definitions.text: it can only just support one

parts.note: a subsistence allowance pays living costs
to crop is to cut

explanation.surface: A benefit has been slashed and barely keeps a person going.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop grown to feed the farmer's household with nothing left to sell.

clue.text: Aid client, being awkward, just the same

indicators.note: awkward suggests something out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Helping a difficult customer is always the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things are exactly alike.

clue.text: Doctor, say, has reduced sediment

parts.note: EG means for example, which is what say means here
has contracted to 's, a reduced form

explanation.surface: A GP, for instance, has cut down on something murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are what settles at the bottom of a drink.

clue.text: Time spent on odd favourite instrument

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Hours spent practising on a quirky, much-loved instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass wind instrument with valves, an example of the class.

clue.text: Article on reform to do it after that point

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: to do it here means to work the letters over, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A piece about reform tells what to do from then on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To do it' rearranges REFORM to REFROM, set after THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefrom means from that place or time onwards.

clue.text: Bring together group of soldiers sent to Spain

parts.note: a unit is a military group
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A regiment is posted abroad to unify forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join or combine.

clue.text: Confine landlord after a drink, which shows malice

indicators.note: after says the next pieces come later in the answer than the drink

parts.note: 'name your poison' means choose a drink
to pen is to confine
a letter is one who lets property

explanation.surface: A drunk landlord is locked up for being spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: The landlord 'lets' rooms, so is a LETTER; in the clue PEN LETTER comes before 'after a drink', which moves it behind POISON.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonymous note written to wound, an example of spiteful mail.

clue.text: Hide here and make attempt to conceal woman

indicators.note: to conceal means to hold inside, so the attempt encloses the woman

parts.note: to try is to make an attempt
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Lie low here, and try to keep a woman out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is an animal skin, treated in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is the workshop where animal skins are made into leather.

clue.text: Broadcasting which is beneath one?

parts.note: beneath one sounds like a snobbish verdict on lowbrow viewing, but the broadcasting arrives through wires laid under the street, below the viewer's feet

explanation.surface: A snob dismisses some kind of programming as unworthy of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beneath one' reads as 'not good enough for me'; literally the service runs through underground cables.
explanation.definitionFit: A television service delivered by wires laid underground, the cryptic reading's literal sense.

clue.text: Wife is in race in turn

indicators.note: in says wife and is go inside the race

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A spouse joins a race and takes their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race, a crossword staple; the second 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a turn or rotation, a synonym.

clue.text: Revolutionary devotees maintain right of dock worker

indicators.note: maintain means hold within, so the rearranged followers enclose the letter for right
revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters of devotees are rearranged

explanation.surface: Radical followers stand up for the rights of a docker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns DEVOTEES into STEVEDOE, and 'maintain' holds R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, a docker by another name.

clue.text: One dead on arrival?

parts.note: dead on arrival sounds like a medical verdict, but 'late' can mean dead, so this is someone who turns up late

explanation.surface: A hospital report on a patient who did not survive the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The late Mr X' means the dead Mr X, so 'dead on arrival' becomes 'late in arriving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arrives after the start, described through 'late' in its sense of deceased.

clue.text: Young woman one repeatedly sent to Russia as an evangelist

parts.note: miss is a young woman
one is given twice, first as the Roman numeral I
and then as the word itself
R is the abbreviation for Russia

explanation.surface: A girl is posted to Russia again and again to preach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' asks for 'one' twice, as I and as ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A missioner is a preacher on a religious mission.

clue.text: Some phraseology psychology uses for a migrant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Academic jargon about the terms used for wandering people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has long been used for a traveller of no fixed abode, a wanderer moving from place to place.

clue.text: Flog off cards where drivers gather?

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of flog are rearranged

parts.note: clubs are one of the card suits

explanation.surface: Sell off playing cards at a motorists' meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' looks like motorists; a driver is also a long-hitting club, kept with others in a golf bag. The phrase also means golf societies.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a kind of golf stick, kept together with the others in the bag.

clue.text: Jump about to conceal name of jurors?

indicators.note: to conceal means to hold something hidden inside, so the turned jump encloses the name letter
about signals turning the word for jump round

parts.note: leap means jump

explanation.surface: A defendant leaps up to hide the identity of those judging the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns LEAP into PAEL, and 'to conceal' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury is a panel, a group sworn to try a case.

clue.text: One easily shocked suppresses the Spanish composition

indicators.note: suppresses means holds down inside, so the shockable person encloses the Spanish article

parts.note: a prude is easily offended
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A prim person bans a Spanish piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is an introductory piece of music.

clue.text: Class accepts learner at university will get in shape twice a month

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the class holds the other pieces

parts.note: a seminar is a class for discussion
L is the learner driver's plate
U stands for university

explanation.surface: A course admits a student who will get fit within a fortnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The moon is half-lit, in a half-moon shape, twice a month, at first and last quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Semilunar means half-moon shaped, the moon's form at each quarter, which comes round twice in a lunar month.

clue.text: The ones left to live round university

definitions.note: a plural phrase for a noun meaning what remains

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for live goes around the university letter

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: Those remaining choose to settle near a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Runner's economy I have followed as a businessman

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, and a river is a runner
a cut is an economy, a saving
I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: A man of business explains how he followed a jogger's thrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a crossword word for river; the Exe flows through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior manager in a company.

clue.text: It can be a good deal painful certainly

definitions.text: It can be a good deal painful certainly

indicators.note: a good deal of the phrase painful certainly holds the letters, so they are taken from within it

explanation.surface: Something hurts a lot, no doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a sore that hurts, and the letters are inside 'painful certainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An open sore in the stomach lining or skin, often very sore.

clue.text: Come in to get chips without fish

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the fish is taken away

parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Enter a chip shop and get chips but no fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips without fish' suggests a takeaway; Chips is sailors' slang for the ship's woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come into a place.

clue.text: Game of cold war criminal

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on a tap
Rudolf Hess, Hitler's deputy, was convicted at Nuremberg

explanation.surface: A Cold War contest with a villain in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two played with kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: Lacking political orthodoxy run off to Spain to get put up

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of run are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
to put up a building is to construct it

explanation.surface: A dissident flees to Spain to be given a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges RUN to UNR; 'put up' looks like giving lodging but means built.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreconstructed person keeps old, unreformed political views.

clue.text: Nero, say, for one in Rome burning

indicators.note: in places the each-word inside the rearranged city
burning suggests destruction, so the letters of Rome are rearranged

parts.note: per means for each one, as in per head

explanation.surface: Nero fiddled while Rome burned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning' rearranges ROME to EMOR; 'in' puts PER (for one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a ruler of the Roman Empire, an example of the title.

clue.text: To dish up meal again could be the speciality of the unforthcoming

definitions.meaning: re- means again and serve means dish up
reticence, holding back, is what unforthcoming people show

explanation.surface: Serving leftovers is the trademark of a shy cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving again is the literal verb; reticence is the noun sense of keeping one's feelings back.
